items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Frank would sit on the bus with a pen, P-E-N, and write chart after — it was like he wrote too many charts almost. I’d say, “Frank, we haven’t learned this other one yet.”

ctx.x: Really and the Vanguard orchestra, I mean it was an inspiration to so many players coming up and writers. That was great stuff.

Sure, absolutely. Well then Frank came on after Thad. Frank Foster. And had a whole different approach to his way of running the band but it was still a great approach. And he was one of the first people who I saw who had so much music coming out of him. He and Thad, you know we always worry as musicians and artists, like is this just a fluke? Am I going to run out of ideas pretty soon? If you can be around some people like that, I mean Frank would sit on the bus with a pen, P-E-N, and write chart after — it was…
Do you regret not finishing college at all?
